title: Spinal injection for back pain
what: The doctor injects a numbing medicine, sometimes with a steroid, near a nerve or a joint of the spine. This reduces pain and inflammation.
why: For severe back or neck pain that spreads to an arm or leg, or a herniated disc, when pills and exercise therapy help little.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes, plus 20 to 30 minutes of observation; the effect lasts from a few hours to several days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will decide if anything needs to change
Allergies to medicines and numbing medicines
Diabetes. The steroid can raise blood sugar
If you have a fever or infection now

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast is usually fine. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Images
prepare.text: Bring your back MRI or CT. They are used to choose the spot.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Your leg may go numb after the procedure. It is best to have someone drive you home.

bring: Your referral and MRI or CT
steps: You lie on your stomach or side
The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
Sometimes the skin is numbed first
The doctor inserts a thin needle, often with X-ray or ultrasound guidance
The needle is removed, and a bandage is put on
You lie for a while under observation
feel: Sometimes your familiar pain gets briefly worse. This means the needle is near the nerve
Warmth or numbness in your back or leg
after: The numbness wears off in a few hours. Be careful when walking
Do not drive on the day of the procedure
For the first 1 to 2 days, the pain may even get worse, then it usually gets better
Keep doing your exercises as your doctor says
red_flags: Weakness in the legs, numbness between the legs, or trouble with peeing or bowel movements: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or severe back pain at the injection site
A severe headache that gets better when you lie down

faq.q: Does the injection cure a herniated disc?
faq.a: No. It relieves pain and inflammation so you can move and continue treatment.

faq.q: How many injections can I have?
faq.a: Your doctor decides. Usually these injections are not done often. Breaks are needed between them.

reminders.text: Spinal injection tomorrow. Bring your back MRI and arrange for someone to drive you home.
